s: A company is replicating an application in a secondary Region. The application usesDynamoDBand RDS for MySQL. The secondary Region must function independently during a disaster.
o: Use DynamoDB global tables and an RDS read replica.
Use DAX and a read replica.
Use global tables and RDS Multi-AZ with standby in secondary Region.
Use Streams and Lambda to copy data. Use read replica.
e: A is correct because: DynamoDB global tables allow for multi-Region, active-active usage. RDS MySQL read replica in another Region supports read workloads and can be promoted during disaster to act as a standalone DB. B is incorrect: DAX is a cache, not a replication mechanism. C is wrong because Multi-AZ doesn't span Regions. D is more manual and error-prone. Reference:https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.ht mlhttps://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html

w.y: The secondary Region must work on its own during a disaster, so both databases need a copy there. DynamoDB global tables keep a full read/write replica in each Region, and an RDS cross-Region read replica can be promoted to a standalone primary.

o.A: Correct: global tables and a cross-Region RDS read replica give independent data copies in the secondary Region.
o.B: DAX is a cache in one Region, not cross-Region replication.
o.C: RDS Multi-AZ standbys are in the same Region, not another Region.
o.D: Custom Streams plus Lambda copying is more work and less reliable than global tables.
